question: What is the primary function of an Electronic Health Record in patient care?

options.A: Managing hospital financial budgets and staff salaries
options.B: Replacing the need for physical nursing assessments completely
options.C: Providing real-time and secure patient data to authorized users
options.D: Storing historical paper charts in digital image format only

explanation: EHRs serve as centralized repositories designed to provide instant access to comprehensive patient information for clinical teams. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why are electronic health records considered superior to traditional paper charts regarding safety?

options.A: They automatically diagnose complex medical conditions without testing
options.B: They eliminate handwriting errors and improve document legibility
options.C: They prevent patients from viewing their own medical history
options.D: They remove the need for nurses to verify medication dosages

explanation: Clear, digital text removes the ambiguity often caused by poor handwriting, which directly prevents medication and transcription mistakes. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which setting utilizes an ambulatory EHR system for patient documentation?
explanation: Ambulatory systems are built for outpatient environments where individuals visit for routine checkups or ongoing chronic care management. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h2)

question: An acute care EHR differs from an ambulatory EHR by focusing primarily on what feature?

options.A: Long-term preventive health tracking over several years
options.B: Rapid inpatient medication administration and continuous monitoring

explanation: Acute care environments require systems that can handle high-acuity interventions, frequent monitoring, and sudden changes in patient status. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is the main advantage of an enterprise EHR system in a large healthcare network?

options.A: Replacing the need for nursing shift handovers
options.B: Connecting multiple facilities into one unified patient database
options.C: Providing specialized pediatric growth charts only
options.D: Lowering the cost of bedside nursing equipment

explanation: Enterprise EHRs bridge disparate locations so patient information travels seamlessly across the entire healthcare system network. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h3)

question: Why would a maternity ward implement a specialty-specific EHR instead of a generic hospital system?

options.A: To reduce the number of registered nurses on duty
options.B: To eliminate the need for physician order entry
options.C: To manage hospital billing and staff payroll
options.D: To utilize customized templates like fetal monitoring strips

explanation: Specialty systems offer tailored data fields that accurately capture clinical details unique to specific medical disciplines. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h3)

question: Who maintains and controls a Personal Health Record (PHR)?
explanation: Unlike hospital-controlled systems, PHRs are managed directly by individuals who choose what information to store and share. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h4)

question: A patient portal is best described as an extension of which system?
explanation: Patient portals link directly to the facility's EHR to give patients secure access to their own clinical notes and test results. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h4)

question: Where is data stored in an on-premise EHR infrastructure?

options.A: On cloud platforms accessed exclusively via the internet
options.B: On remote servers managed by external software vendors
options.C: Inside personal mobile phones of the nursing staff
options.D: On physical servers located inside the healthcare facility

explanation: On-premise setups keep all hardware and data storage locally within the physical building of the hospital or clinic. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h5)

question: A rural clinic experiencing frequent internet downtime is advised to carefully evaluate which EHR infrastructure type?

options.A: Ambulatory portals because they eliminate clinical documentation
options.B: Cloud-based systems due to reliance on continuous internet access
options.C: On-premise systems because they do not require any electricity
options.D: Personal health records because they replace hospital databases

explanation: Cloud solutions depend heavily on stable internet connectivity, making them vulnerable in environments with unreliable network infrastructure. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h5)

question: What does EHR interoperability primarily allow different systems to do?

options.A: Automatically print paper charts for every patient
options.B: Communicate and exchange patient data accurately
options.C: Eliminate the need for nursing documentation completely
options.D: Lower the financial cost of purchasing computer hardware

explanation: Interoperability ensures that separate software platforms can share clinical information smoothly without data corruption. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the main clinical risk when an EHR system lacks proper interoperability?

options.A: Hospital pharmacies run out of essential emergency drugs
options.B: Patient information remains trapped in isolated digital silos
options.C: Nurses spend extra time administering bedside medications
options.D: Physicians are forced to use paper charts permanently

explanation: Without interoperability, data cannot travel between different hospital networks, leaving care teams blind to previous medical history. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h6)

question: How does Bar Code Medication Administration integrated within an EHR improve patient safety?

options.A: It calculates the exact financial cost of each prescribed pill
options.B: It automatically prescribes medications without physician review
options.C: It cross-checks the patient wristband with the drug package
options.D: It replaces the physical nursing assessment of vital signs

explanation: BCMA technology provides a final electronic barrier against medication errors right before administration occurs at the bedside. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h7)

question: What negative clinical behavior can result from poorly designed EHR alerts and alarms?

options.A: Alert fatigue leading nurses to ignore important warnings
options.B: Faster documentation speeds during emergency trauma care
options.C: Improved communication between doctors and pharmacists
options.D: Increased compliance with hospital handoff protocols

explanation: Too many non-urgent pop-up warnings cause clinicians to tune out alerts, increasing the risk of missing critical safety notifications. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h7)
